text: Reproduction validated (3/3 detections, 0 false alarms). Writing the atomic-update fix.

checks.name: same_behaviour
checks.detail: 40 sequential requests matched the original exactly

args.root_cause: Read-modify-write lost update: deposit/withdraw SELECT the balance in autocommit-level READ COMMITTED, compute balance +/- amount in Python, then UPDATE the absolute value. Two concurrent requests on the same account both read the same balance and both write back the same adjusted value, so one update silently overwrites the other. No error is raised, so reconciliation (balance vs sum of successful ops) drifts.
args.fix: Make each update a single atomic SQL statement: deposit uses UPDATE ... SET balance = balance + %s WHERE id=%s RETURNING; withdraw uses UPDATE ... SET balance = balance - %s WHERE id=%s AND balance >= %s RETURNING, letting the row lock serialise only contenders on the same account and the deduction be computed from the current row. On no row updated during withdraw, an EXISTS probe inside the same transaction preserves the original errors exactly: ValueError for unknown accounts, InsufficientFunds otherwise. Sequential behaviour (unknown account, overdraft rejection without changing the balance, CHECK constraint) is unchanged.

text: Fix accepted. Root cause was a read-modify-write lost update; fixed with single-statement atomic increments/decrements guarded by `balance >= amount`.
